operator_shape: PM08 is a historical review-only note: never applied, never executed, never credited with a kill. No source assertion (literal or AST) is made for it, and no static transition is asserted. The inventory holds 11 entries: 10 executable mutants plus 1 manual review note.
supersedes: inventory version 2 (the AST proposal in fixes/MutationEvidence/, kept filed as a snapshot; its AST gate is not shipped)

mutation_semantics_changed_vs_v2.PM08-no-lazy-fetch-review-only: the AST tuple-membership gate and the static_check/alternatives are removed: the entry is review-only, no mutant is built, no grid invocation is made, no kill is credited, and no source assertion is made for it.

mutants_v3.attribution_basis: every cell whose audited repository is promisor-marked: a refusal on the metadata alone turns each of them into exit 2
mutants_v3.semantic: promisor metadata alone (extensions.partialClone, remote.*.promisor, partialclonefilter, paired .promisor+.pack) is not a refusal: a complete promisor-marked repository keeps the verdict of its full-clone twin

mutants_v3.attribution_basis: every cell with an unresolved citation whose ordinary verdict is a failed finding: the errata-corrected absent hash is refused before the ledger is consulted, and the opaque cells misclassify an absence that a missing tree may conceal
mutants_v3.semantic: the unknown rule covers a locally unresolved citation that names unavailable referenced content; it must not cover every absent citation, or the historical errata-marked clone (absent hash corrected by errata) would stop being an ordinary failed finding. The mutant refuses every absent (or unknown) citation, before the errata ledger is consulted.

mutants_v3.attribution_basis: every cell whose required evidence is unavailable and whose verdict must be could-not-evaluate
mutants_v3.semantic: objects the audit actually reads must be available: a missing required commit/tree/blob/report object is could-not-evaluate (exit 2), never a clean or failed verdict. This mutant removes the store's missing-object computation (the completeness element); PM04 removes the decision that uses it. Both attack the same verdict surface, so the grid kills them alike: one of them surviving is not evidence about the other.

mutants_v3.attribution_basis: every cell whose unresolved citation names unavailable referenced content
mutants_v3.semantic: a locally unresolved citation that names unavailable referenced local content is could-not-evaluate rather than proved absent; the mutant accepts it as absent and reports an ordinary failed finding

mutants_v3.attribution_basis: every cell whose citation resolves only in the second audited repository
mutants_v3.semantic: a citation missing in one audited repository but present in the other audited repository is resolvable; the mutant consults the first repository only

mutants_v3.attribution_basis: every cell whose verdict must be could-not-evaluate because a required read failed
mutants_v3.semantic: a failing read of the object the audit needs is could-not-evaluate; the mutant swallows the failure and guesses a value, turning an unavailable object into a verdict

mutants_v3.attribution_basis: every cell with a hole the audit does not need: an unrelated hole must not refuse the audit
mutants_v3.semantic: the missing-object traversal is rooted at the pinned lane/fleet roots the audit reads; the mutant roots it at --all. Redundant on a candidate whose traversal already starts from every present object: there it is observationally identical, survives, and is credited with no kill.

review-only note, uncredited: every git call carries --no-lazy-fetch, so a missing promisor object can never be fetched through the promisor remote (transport, repository programs, signatures). This element is not part of the executed inventory: no mutant is built, no grid invocation is made for it, and it is never credited with a kill

mutants_v3.attribution_basis: every cell whose locally present blob must stay an ordinary wrong-type finding
mutants_v3.semantic: the bare full-hash lookup stays unpeeled: a citation of a locally present blob resolves as found; peeling it to ^{commit} turns a present blob into a missing object

mutants_v3.attribution_basis: every cell whose verdict depends on the opaque non-leaf rule
mutants_v3.semantic: when a citation is unresolved, a missing tree or commit may conceal the dependency names, so the citation is unevaluable (exit 2); the mutant ignores that hole and reports an ordinary failed finding. A known-present blob that merely fails commit peeling keeps its wrong-type finding either way.

mutants_v3.attribution_basis: every cell whose audited repository holds a hole, whatever verdict the cell expects: the gate is unconditional
mutants_v3.semantic: no missing-object state may be an unconditional audit precondition: an unrelated blob hole next to a fabricated citation keeps the ordinary failed finding, and an unused tree hole next to fully resolved citations keeps the clean verdict; the mutant refuses on any hole
